title: On the Welfare Costs of Naiveté in the US Credit-Card Market
abstract: We argue that in addition to the textbook exploitation of consumers, the presence of naive consumers leads to a participation distortion in competitive markets, since the additional profits from naive consumers lead competitive firms to lower transparent prices below cost in order to attract these consumers.
